passages.text: Not many of you should become teachers, my brothers, because you know that we who teach will be judged more strictly.
passages.original: Μὴ πολλοὶ διδάσκαλοι γίνεσθε ἀδελφοί μου εἰδότες ὅτι μεῖζον κρίμα λημψόμεθα
passages.objections:
I think anyone who wants to teach should just go ahead and do it—there’s no real risk.
Why shouldn’t everyone try to be a teacher? It’s the best way to get respect in the community.
If I know a little bit, that’s enough to start teaching others, right?
There’s no difference between being a teacher and any other role in the church.
God doesn’t care if I make mistakes while teaching; it’s not a big deal.
I don’t need to worry about being held accountable for what I say when I teach.
Teaching is easy—there’s nothing special or serious about it.
As long as I have good intentions, it doesn’t matter if I become a teacher.
Everyone should try to be a leader or teacher, no matter their experience or knowledge.
There’s no extra responsibility that comes with teaching others about faith.

passages.text: We all stumble in many ways. If anyone is never at fault in what he says, he is a perfect man, able to control his whole body.
passages.original: πολλὰ γὰρ πταίομεν ἅπαντες εἴ τις ἐν λόγῳ οὐ πταίει οὗτος τέλειος ἀνήρ δυνατὸς χαλιναγωγῆσαι καὶ ὅλον τὸ σῶμα
passages.objections:
I never make mistakes, especially not with my words.
Some people are just naturally perfect and never say anything wrong.
If I can control what I say, then I must be flawless in every other part of my life too.
Only really bad people ever stumble or mess up.
Once you become wise, you’ll never say anything foolish again.
I don’t need to worry about my words; they don’t really matter that much.
If someone is good at speaking, that means they’re perfect in every way.
I’ve never hurt anyone with my words, so I must be completely righteous.
People who make mistakes with their words just aren’t trying hard enough.
It’s possible to live your whole life without ever slipping up in what you say.

passages.text: When we put bits into the mouths of horses to make them obey us, we can guide the whole animal.
passages.original: Εἰ δὲ τῶν ἵππων τοὺς χαλινοὺς εἰς τὰ στόματα βάλλομεν εἰς τὸ πείθεσθαι αὐτοὺς ἡμῖν καὶ ὅλον τὸ σῶμα αὐτῶν μετάγομεν
passages.objections:
It doesn’t matter what I say; my words don’t really affect my actions.
I can’t control myself, so there’s no point in trying to change how I speak.
What I say isn’t important compared to what I do with my body.
Small things like words can’t possibly influence my whole life.
No one can really guide their behavior just by watching their tongue.
It’s impossible for something so little to have any real power over me.
My speech is separate from the rest of who I am.
If I mess up with my words, it won’t affect anything else about me.
There’s no way to steer my life by just changing how I talk.
Only big actions matter; little things like speech are insignificant.

passages.text: Consider ships as well. Although they are so large and are driven by strong winds, they are steered by a very small rudder wherever the pilot is inclined.
passages.original: ἰδοὺ καὶ τὰ πλοῖα τηλικαῦτα ὄντα καὶ ὑπὸ ἀνέμων σκληρῶν ἐλαυνόμενα μετάγεται ὑπὸ ἐλαχίστου πηδαλίου ὅπου ἡ ὁρμὴ τοῦ εὐθύνοντος βούλεται
passages.objections:
It doesn’t matter what I say; my words can’t really change anything in my life.
I’m just one person—my actions and choices are too small to make a difference.
Big problems in life are impossible to steer or control, no matter what I do.
Small things don’t matter when you’re facing huge challenges.
I can’t influence the direction of my life; everything is up to fate or luck.
There’s no point in trying to guide my life when so many forces are against me.
Minor habits or words don’t have any real impact on the bigger picture.
I’m powerless to change course once things get out of hand.
Only big, dramatic actions can change the direction of my life.
Little things I do or say are insignificant compared to the storms I face.

passages.text: In the same way, the tongue is a small part of the body, but it boasts of great things. Consider how small a spark sets a great forest ablaze.
passages.original: Οὕτως καὶ ἡ γλῶσσα μικρὸν μέλος ἐστὶν καὶ μεγάλα αὐχεῖ ἰδοὺ ἡλίκον πῦρ ἡλίκην ὕλην ἀνάπτει
passages.objections:
It’s just words—what harm can they really do?
My speech doesn’t matter; it’s my actions that count.
Nobody pays attention to what I say anyway.
A little gossip here and there won’t hurt anyone.
I can say whatever I want; it won’t have any real consequences.
It’s not like my insults or jokes can actually cause any damage.
Words are harmless compared to physical actions.
I don’t need to watch my mouth; people should just toughen up.
If I’m just venting, it’s not a big deal.
There’s no way something so small as my tongue could cause real trouble.

passages.text: The tongue also is a fire, a world of wickedness among the parts of the body. It pollutes the whole person, sets the course of his life on fire, and is itself set on fire by hell.
passages.original: καὶ ἡ γλῶσσα πῦρ ὁ κόσμος τῆς ἀδικίας ἡ γλῶσσα καθίσταται ἐν τοῖς μέλεσιν ἡμῶν ἡ σπιλοῦσα ὅλον τὸ σῶμα καὶ φλογίζουσα τὸν τροχὸν τῆς γενέσεως καὶ φλογιζομένη ὑπὸ τῆς γεέννης
passages.objections:
Words don’t really matter; it’s only actions that count.
I can say whatever I want—my speech doesn’t affect my life.
It’s impossible for what I say to truly harm me or others.
My tongue isn’t dangerous; it’s just a small part of me.
There’s no real consequence to speaking harshly or spreading rumors.
I can control everything about myself, so my words can’t get out of hand.
Speaking evil or lies is harmless as long as I don’t act on them.
No one’s ever been ruined by what they say—only by what they do.
My words can’t possibly influence the direction of my life.
It’s not a big deal if I curse or insult others; it doesn’t affect my soul.

passages.text: All kinds of animals, birds, reptiles, and creatures of the sea are being tamed and have been tamed by man, but no man can tame the tongue. It is a restless evil, full of deadly poison.
passages.original: Πᾶσα γὰρ φύσις θηρίων τε καὶ πετεινῶν ἑρπετῶν τε καὶ ἐναλίων δαμάζεται καὶ δεδάμασται τῇ φύσει τῇ ἀνθρωπίνῃ τὴν δὲ γλῶσσαν οὐδεὶς δαμάσαι δύναται ἀνθρώπων ἀκατάστατον κακόν μεστὴ ἰοῦ θανατηφόρου
passages.objections:
I think if I just try hard enough, I can control everything I say perfectly.
People can master their words just like they train animals; it’s just a matter of discipline.
Once you’re wise enough, your tongue will never get you into trouble again.
If I’m a good person, I’ll never say anything harmful or wrong.
There’s no real danger in what we say; words don’t have that much power.
I don’t need to worry about my speech—my intentions are always good, so my words can’t hurt anyone.
Anyone can completely tame their tongue if they really want to.
It’s only the truly wicked who ever say anything poisonous or evil.
I’ve never said anything I regret, so I must have full control over my tongue.
Once you become a believer, your words will always be pure and harmless.

passages.text: With the tongue we bless our Lord and Father, and with it we curse men, who have been made in God’s likeness.
passages.original: Ἐν αὐτῇ εὐλογοῦμεν τὸν Κύριον καὶ Πατέρα καὶ ἐν αὐτῇ καταρώμεθα τοὺς ἀνθρώπους τοὺς καθ’ ὁμοίωσιν Θεοῦ γεγονότας
passages.objections:
I don’t see any harm in speaking badly about others if they’ve wronged me.
It’s fine to praise God and then insult people; they’re not the same thing.
If someone annoys me, I have every right to curse them, no matter who they are.
My words to people don’t matter as long as I’m respectful to God.
People aren’t that important, so it doesn’t matter what I say about them.
I can separate my worship from how I treat others with my words.
It’s impossible to control what I say when I’m angry, so it shouldn’t count against me.
Some people deserve to be cursed, even if I claim to love God.
As long as I’m honest, it’s okay to speak harshly about others.
God only cares about my prayers, not how I talk to other people.

passages.text: Out of the same mouth come blessing and cursing. My brothers, this should not be!
passages.original: ἐκ τοῦ αὐτοῦ στόματος ἐξέρχεται εὐλογία καὶ κατάρα οὐ χρή ἀδελφοί μου ταῦτα οὕτως γίνεσθαι
passages.objections:
I don’t see any harm in speaking kindly to some people and harshly to others—it’s just being real.
It’s impossible to always control what I say; sometimes people just deserve to be cursed out.
Why should I worry about my words? As long as I praise God, it doesn’t matter how I talk to others.
I can’t help it if I bless my friends and curse my enemies—that’s just how life works.
Isn’t it normal to speak good and bad things? Everyone does it, so what’s the problem?
If someone wrongs me, I have every right to curse them, even if I also pray to God.
My words don’t really matter as long as my heart is in the right place.
I can separate my faith from how I talk to people; they’re not connected.
It’s not realistic to expect anyone to always speak kindly—sometimes you have to be harsh.
Why should I be held responsible for every word I say?

passages.text: Can both fresh water and salt water flow from the same spring?
passages.original: μήτι ἡ πηγὴ ἐκ τῆς αὐτῆς ὀπῆς βρύει τὸ γλυκὺ καὶ τὸ πικρόν
passages.objections:
I can say whatever I want, and it doesn’t matter if I bless some people and curse others.
It’s fine to act one way at church and a completely different way at home.
Nobody will notice if I’m kind one moment and cruel the next.
It’s natural to have both good and bad words come from the same person.
I can’t help it if I sometimes speak harshly; that’s just how people are.
As long as I do some good things, it doesn’t matter if I also do some bad things.
My words don’t really reflect what’s in my heart.
It’s impossible to be consistent in how we treat others.
I can praise God and insult my neighbor without any problem.
There’s no harm in mixing good and bad behavior—it’s just being human.

passages.text: My brothers, can a fig tree grow olives, or a grapevine bear figs? Neither can a salt spring produce fresh water.
passages.original: μὴ δύναται ἀδελφοί μου συκῆ ἐλαίας ποιῆσαι ἢ ἄμπελος σῦκα οὔτε ἁλυκὸν γλυκὺ ποιῆσαι ὕδωρ
passages.objections:
I think I can live however I want and still be a good person inside.
It's fine if my words and actions don't match—nobody's perfect.
I can say whatever I want, even if it's hurtful, as long as I do good things sometimes.
My background doesn't matter; I can just change who I am whenever I feel like it.
It's possible to have both good and bad coming from the same place in my heart.
I can follow God and still hold onto my old, selfish ways.
I don't need to worry about what kind of person I am deep down, as long as I look good on the outside.
I can mix a little bit of truth with lies and it will still be okay.
My actions don't really show what's in my heart.
I can be one person at church and a completely different person everywhere else.

passages.text: Who is wise and understanding among you? Let him show it by his good conduct, by deeds done in the humility that comes from wisdom.
passages.original: Τίς σοφὸς καὶ ἐπιστήμων ἐν ὑμῖν δειξάτω ἐκ τῆς καλῆς ἀναστροφῆς τὰ ἔργα αὐτοῦ ἐν πραΰτητι σοφίας
passages.objections:
If someone is really wise, they don’t need to prove it by how they act—just knowing things is enough.
I can be considered wise just because I have a lot of knowledge, even if my actions don’t always match up.
It doesn’t matter how I treat others as long as I have the right answers and can outsmart everyone.
Humility isn’t important for someone who’s truly wise; it’s better to show off what you know.
People will respect me for my wisdom even if I act arrogantly or harshly.
Good deeds aren’t necessary to prove understanding; words alone should be enough.
Wisdom is about being clever and getting ahead, not about being gentle or kind.
I can be wise and still act selfishly or rudely—my behavior doesn’t affect my reputation.
As long as I have the right beliefs, my conduct doesn’t really matter.
It’s okay to use my knowledge to put others down, because that’s what makes me look smart.

passages.text: But if you harbor bitter jealousy and selfish ambition in your hearts, do not boast in it or deny the truth.
passages.original: εἰ δὲ ζῆλον πικρὸν ἔχετε καὶ ἐριθείαν ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ ὑμῶν μὴ κατακαυχᾶσθε καὶ ψεύδεσθε κατὰ τῆς ἀληθείας
passages.objections:
I don’t see anything wrong with being jealous if it gets me ahead.
If I want something someone else has, why shouldn’t I go after it, no matter what?
It’s fine to brag about my achievements, even if I had to step on others to get there.
A little selfishness is necessary if you want to succeed in this world.
If I hide my true motives, no one gets hurt, right?
There’s nothing wrong with twisting the truth if it makes me look better.
Why shouldn’t I boast about my ambitions? It shows I’m confident.
If I feel bitter toward others, that’s just being honest with myself.
Ambition is always good, even if it means putting others down.
Jealousy just means I care enough to compete; it’s not a bad thing.

passages.text: Such wisdom does not come from above, but is earthly, unspiritual, demonic.
passages.original: οὐκ ἔστιν αὕτη ἡ σοφία ἄνωθεν κατερχομένη ἀλλὰ ἐπίγειος ψυχική δαιμονιώδης
passages.objections:
I think if I’m clever enough to get ahead, it must be a sign that I’m blessed.
Isn’t it wise to do whatever it takes to win, even if it means stepping on others?
All wisdom comes from within myself, not from any higher source.
If I’m successful and powerful, that proves my way is the right way.
Why shouldn’t I trust my own instincts and desires above everything else?
I don’t see any problem with using manipulation to get what I want.
Isn’t it just practical to look out for myself first?
If I can outsmart others, that’s just being wise, isn’t it?
There’s nothing wrong with a little selfish ambition if it gets results.
I don’t need any guidance from above; I can figure things out on my own.

passages.text: For where jealousy and selfish ambition exist, there will be disorder and every evil practice.
passages.original: ὅπου γὰρ ζῆλος καὶ ἐριθεία ἐκεῖ ἀκαταστασία καὶ πᾶν φαῦλον πρᾶγμα
passages.objections:
I don’t see any harm in a little competition and wanting to get ahead of others.
Jealousy just means I care about what’s mine—how could that lead to anything bad?
If I put myself first, everything else will fall into place for everyone.
Ambition is always a good thing, no matter what motivates it.
People only fight because of outside problems, not because of what’s in their hearts.
As long as I get what I want, it doesn’t matter if others are jealous or upset.
Selfishness is just being practical in this world.
Disorder only happens when people don’t follow the rules, not because of jealousy or ambition.
It’s normal to want what others have; it doesn’t cause any real trouble.
If I’m ambitious, it means I’m wise and strong, not that I’m doing anything wrong.

passages.text: But the wisdom from above is first of all pure, then peace-loving, gentle, accommodating, full of mercy and good fruit, impartial, and sincere.
passages.original: Ἡ δὲ ἄνωθεν σοφία πρῶτον μὲν ἁγνή ἐστιν ἔπειτα εἰρηνική ἐπιεικής εὐπειθής μεστὴ ἐλέους καὶ καρπῶν ἀγαθῶν ἀδιάκριτος ἀνυπόκριτος
passages.objections:
If you want to get ahead in this world, you have to be ruthless and look out for yourself first.
Mercy and gentleness just make you weak—people will walk all over you if you act like that.
It’s impossible to be fair to everyone; you have to pick sides and show favoritism to get by.
Nobody really cares if you’re sincere or not, as long as you get results.
Being peaceful and accommodating just means you’re avoiding conflict and not standing up for yourself.
You can’t trust people who act gentle—they’re probably hiding something.
If you want to be wise, you need to be cunning and know how to manipulate situations.
Showing mercy is a waste; people need to learn from their mistakes the hard way.
True wisdom is about being tough and never letting your guard down.
It’s better to pretend to be good than to actually be sincere—appearances are what matter.

passages.text: Peacemakers who sow in peace reap the fruit of righteousness.
passages.original: καρπὸς δὲ δικαιοσύνης ἐν εἰρήνῃ σπείρεται τοῖς ποιοῦσιν εἰρήνην
passages.objections:
Fighting back is the only way to get what’s rightfully mine.
If I don’t stand up for myself with force, no one will respect me.
Making peace just means letting others walk all over you.
Nothing good ever comes from trying to keep the peace; it’s a waste of time.
People who avoid conflict are just weak and get taken advantage of.
You have to be aggressive if you want to see any real change.
Why bother trying to make peace when everyone else is just looking out for themselves?
If I forgive and try to make peace, I’ll just lose out in the end.
Only the strongest survive, not the peacemakers.
Righteousness comes from winning battles, not from making peace.
